names.official: Republic of the Union of Myanmar

summary: Nationals of 100 countries can apply for Myanmar's official tourist eVisa — 28 days, US$50, valid only for arrival at the Yangon, Mandalay and Nay Pyi Taw international airports or the Kawthaung land border — while Brunei, Cambodian, Indonesian, Lao, Philippine, Thai, Vietnamese and Singaporean passport holders enter visa-free for short stays. Canada says land crossings may close with little or no notice or be restricted to nationals of neighbouring states, and the UK advises against all travel to much of the country.

notes: The UK government says there are strict regulations on bringing in and using drones: do not try to enter Myanmar with one unless you have the permits before you travel. Australia's Smartraveller says drones have been seized by customs and tourists arrested for flying them.

You must declare gold, gems and jewellery to customs on arrival, and you cannot import gold for trading (UK government). Canada says exporting gems is illegal and a permit is needed to buy or possess cultural or archaeological artefacts.

payments.text: The UK government says Myanmar is largely a cash-based society: many ATMs do not accept international cards, many shops take only cash, and you should phone ahead if you want to pay a hotel or restaurant by card. Canada says US dollars are widely accepted but only as new, unmarked, undamaged notes, and that changing money anywhere other than an authorised exchange is illegal.

safety.text: Canada says the armed conflict has continued to escalate since the military seized control in February 2021, and strongly advises against all travel to Myanmar; the UK advises against all travel to much of the country. Canada reports regime airstrikes and drone strikes causing civilian casualties; the UK says some areas are under martial law or curfews, and both warn of a risk of arbitrary detention.

tips.text: Canada strongly advises against all travel to Myanmar and Australia says do not travel; the UK advises against all travel to much of the country, including Rakhine, Kachin, Chin and Shan North, and against all but essential travel to Mandalay Region. Canada reports regime airstrikes and drone strikes, and says embassy staff need government permission to travel outside Yangon.

Canada advises against all travel to Myanmar, including through its land borders, and says crossings may close with little or no notice or be restricted to nationals of the neighbouring state. The eVisa is valid only for arrival at Yangon, Mandalay and Nay Pyi Taw international airports and the Kawthaung land checkpoint.

The UK government says Myanmar is largely cash-based and many ATMs do not accept international cards, that US dollar notes must be in good condition, without pen marks, folds or tears, and that exchange counters may refuse notes whose serial numbers start AB or CB.

The UK government says the authorities control internet access and periodically cut it off entirely, and that some services, including Facebook and WhatsApp, are blocked. Canada advises charging your phone and carrying power banks in case of internet, communication and power outages.
The UK government says to remove shoes and socks before entering a pagoda or monastery, and that shorts, short skirts and sleeveless tops can cause offence at religious sites.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Myanmar?
faq.answer: Yes, unless you hold a Brunei, Cambodian, Indonesian, Lao, Philippine or Thai passport (14 days visa-free through the main international airports) or a Vietnamese or Singaporean one (30 days). Nationals of 100 countries — including the US, the UK, every EU country and Australia — can apply for the 28-day tourist eVisa (US$50) at evisa.moip.gov.mm; others apply at a Myanmar embassy or consulate.

faq.question: Can I enter Myanmar overland?
faq.answer: Canada advises against all travel to Myanmar, including through its land borders, and says crossings may close with little or no notice or be restricted to nationals of the neighbouring state. The eVisa is valid only at Yangon, Mandalay and Nay Pyi Taw international airports and the Kawthaung land checkpoint.

faq.question: Is Myanmar safe to visit?
faq.answer: Canada strongly advises against all travel to Myanmar and Australia says do not travel; the UK advises against all travel to much of the country. Canada reports an escalating conflict with regime airstrikes, drone strikes and civilian casualties, and says improvised explosive devices have been used in Yangon, Mandalay and Nay Pyi Taw.

faq.question: How long does the Myanmar eVisa take?
faq.answer: Processing takes at least 3 working days (Myanmar time), counted from the acknowledgement email sent after you submit and pay. The official portal is evisa.moip.gov.mm. You must print the approval letter and show it on arrival.

faq.question: Can I extend a Myanmar tourist visa?
faq.answer: No. The official eVisa FAQ says the tourist eVisa cannot be extended; only a business eVisa can be extended, through the eStay system. No official source we could read states the overstay penalty.
